posts.title: 2026.33: The CapEx Train Keeps Rolling
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of August 10, 2026, including the capital constraint, AI writing, and a tale of two cities.
bullets: Nvidia is implementing new financial engineering mechanisms to secure long-duration capital, signaling potential concerns regarding the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.
The reliance on creative funding models and equity taps by major players like Google suggests that AI compute investments are not yet generating sufficient organic returns to cover their own costs.
New EU regulations mandating the labeling of AI-generated content face criticism for potentially stifling innovation and failing to account for the evolving societal acceptance of synthetic media.

The divergence between New York City's resilient financial sector and Hollywood's declining production base highlights how network effects can protect some industries while leaving others vulnerable to geographic outsourcing.

posts.title: Li Auto's chip ambitions extend from assisted driving to data centers, report says
posts.summary:
Li Auto is exploring an in-house cloud inference chip, and the project is still at an early stage.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto is in the early stages of developing an in-house cloud inference chip to handle workloads currently managed by GPUs.
The project aims to leverage the dataflow architecture used in the company's vehicle-side assisted driving chips to reduce R&D costs through shared design and software tools.
While technically feasible, the company faces significant challenges in achieving cost-competitive inference performance compared to established cloud infrastructure providers.
The initiative reflects a broader trend of automotive companies seeking vertical integration in AI hardware to optimize both vehicle performance and backend data processing.

posts.title: Li Auto's L6 tops 400,000 cumulative deliveries as revamped model revives demand
posts.summary:
The Li L6 delivered about 9,000 units in the first half of August, compared with just 2,716 for the whole of July, based on CnEVPost-compiled data.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Li Auto's L6 SUV has surpassed 400,000 cumulative deliveries in less than 27 months, cementing its status as a critical volume driver for the company.
Demand for the model has rebounded significantly following the July 16 launch of a revamped version, with deliveries reaching approximately 9,000 units in the first half of August.
The updated L6 features substantial technical upgrades, including a 51 kWh battery for a 300 km all-electric range and the integration of the in-house Mach M100 assisted driving chip.
The successful refresh of the L6 is a central component of Li Auto's broader strategy to modernize its L-series extended-range electric vehicle lineup to combat slowing demand for older models.

posts.title: Geely Farizon's first overseas plant starts operations in Indonesia
posts.summary:
The first locally assembled V8E all-electric logistics vehicle rolled off the line on August 13 at a plant about 80 kilometers southeast of Jakarta.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Farizon has commenced operations at its first overseas knock-down (KD) plant in Indonesia, located southeast of Jakarta.
The facility has begun local assembly of the V8E all-electric logistics vehicle, which has been specifically calibrated for local road conditions and tropical climates.
This move represents a strategic shift from pure vehicle exports to localized production, aimed at bypassing tariffs and meeting tightening local content requirements in Southeast Asia.
The company plans to gradually expand its localized product lineup and integrate further into the Indonesian industrial supply chain.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Lam Research and ASE expansions; data center shifts; CPO system architecture initiative; 2D-transistor interface solution; USENIX HW security; patent suits; image sensors; programmable AI memtransistor; Nvidia's new plan; earnings; Tier IV's L4 auto chip.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: ASE subsidiary SPIL is investing $3.1 billion in a new Taiwan-based facility to expand CoWoS capacity for AI chips, with production slated to begin in 2028.

Data center infrastructure is undergoing a critical architectural shift toward 1-megawatt racks, necessitating fundamental changes in power delivery, cooling, and 3D-IC packaging to support AI workloads.
Rhodium Group projects that China's legacy semiconductor capacity will approach 50% of global output by 2030, even as the nation faces ongoing restrictions on leading-edge AI chip technology.
Lam Research announced a $3 billion, five-year R&D expansion plan to increase its experimental capacity by over 50%, alongside a new workforce development partnership with NY Creates.
Industry experts are increasingly advocating for smaller, open-source AI models that can run on local hardware, potentially reducing the reliance on massive, energy-intensive data centers.
